stem:
Meena wraps an insulated copper wire around an iron nail and connects the ends to a cell to make an electromagnet for a school project. She uses it to pick up steel paper clips.
Which statement about her electromagnet is correct?

options.text: The nail stays magnetised and keeps holding the clips even after the current is switched off.
The iron nail inside the coil makes the electromagnet weaker.
Without the iron nail, the current-carrying coil cannot behave like a magnet at all.
The current-carrying coil behaves like a magnet, and the iron nail inside the coil makes the electromagnet stronger.

teacher.key_rationale: A current-carrying coil acts as a temporary magnet, and an iron core concentrates the magnetic field, making the electromagnet stronger; the clips fall when the current stops. D states both facts correctly. A wrongly claims permanent magnetism, B reverses the strengthening effect of the core, and C wrongly claims the bare coil has no magnetic effect.
